root_cause.text: The MPTCP in-kernel path manager did not increment `msk->pm.local_addr_used` for endpoints with both `signal` and `subflow` flags when subflow creation was impossible due to limits, while still clearing the corresponding bit in `msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap` upon sending ADD_ADDR, creating an inconsistency that triggered a warning when removing the endpoint.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "In this case, msk->pm.local_addr_used has been kept to 0 -- because no subflows have been created -- but the corresponding bit in msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap has been cleared when the ADD_ADDR has been sent." The patch adds `msk->pm.local_addr_used++` inside the `exit` section when `signal_and_subflow` is set and subflows were not created, to keep the counter consistent with the bitmap.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing increment of local_addr_used for endpoints with both signal and subflow flags when subflow creation is not possible, to avoid accounting errors on endpoint removal.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional increment of msk->pm.local_addr_used at the exit of mptcp_pm_create_subflow_or_signal_addr when an endpoint has both signal and subflow flags but no subflows were created (while loop did not execute) and the endpoint ID differs from the MPC endpoint ID.
intent_record.how: This ensures that the local_addr_used counter is correctly incremented for endpoints that are both signal and subflow even when no subflow creation occurs, preventing accounting mismatches when later calling __mark_subflow_endp_available() during endpoint removal.
